newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Randex buys 9.1 pct stake in Rareco.
newsitem.headline: Randex buys 9.1 pct stake in Rareco.

text.p: Randex Ltd said on Monday it had bought a 9.1 percent stake in Rare Earth Extraction Co Ltd (Rareco) for three million rand, in line with its policy of investing in attractive small mining development opportunities.

It said the acquisition was effected by Randex subscribing for new shares in Rareco which owns 50 percent of a rare earth magnet production facility in the Western Cape and a mining license for a monazite mine in the Northern Cape province.
Neil Gardyne, a director of Randex said Rareco had the potential to develop from the rapid growth of the rare earths minerals industry.
"Randex looks to these investments (in small to medium-sized operations) to establish a solid earnings base over time to expand our development operations," he said.

Rare earth products, the majority of which are extracted from minerals monazite and bastnaesite, are used in specialised applications including robotics, computer hard disk drives and vehicle braking systems.
Rareco plans to produce up to 12,000 tonnes of monazite a year by 1999, the financing of which would be announced shortly.
